topic.label: Civil Engineering
topic.desc: Civil Engineering: the analysis, design and construction of structures, foundations, water systems and transportation networks.

concepts: Analysis and design of beams, frames, trusses and slabs so that load paths, stresses and deflections stay within code limits.
Behaviour of soil and rock as engineering materials, covering site investigation, bearing capacity, settlement and slope stability.
Flow of water in pipes, channels and catchments, used to design drainage, flood control and water supply systems.
Planning, geometric design and operation of roads, rail and transit so that traffic moves safely and efficiently.
Planning, scheduling, costing and safe execution of civil works from tender to handover.
Properties and testing of concrete, steel, asphalt and timber used in civil infrastructure.
skills: Computes member forces, moments and deflections for a frame or truss under specified load combinations and checks equilibrium at every joint.
Sizes steel and reinforced concrete members for bending, shear and axial load and checks each against the governing design code clauses.
Assembles dead, live, wind and seismic load cases into factored combinations and verifies factors against the referenced standard.
Calculates allowable bearing pressure for shallow foundations from soil strength parameters and checks the factor of safety.
Estimates immediate and consolidation settlement from borehole and laboratory data and compares totals with tolerable limits.
Evaluates slope stability with limit-equilibrium methods and reports the critical slip surface and factor of safety for review.
Solves flows and pressures in a water distribution network and checks that continuity and energy balance close at every node.
Estimates peak runoff from a catchment using rainfall intensity and land cover and checks results against a second method.
Sizes open channels and culverts with Manning flow relations and checks velocity and freeboard limits.
Computes level of service and delay at intersections and road segments from traffic counts and checks inputs for consistency.
Lays out horizontal and vertical alignment with curve radii and sight distances and checks each element against design speed rules.
Selects pavement layer thicknesses from traffic loading and subgrade strength and verifies the design life calculation.
Builds an activity network, computes the critical path and float, and checks that logic links and durations are complete.
Takes off quantities from drawings, prices them and reconciles the total against unit-rate benchmarks.
Identifies construction hazards for each work stage and checks the safety plan against applicable regulations.
Proportions cement, water, aggregate and admixtures for a target strength and checks the water-cement ratio and durability limits.
Interprets cylinder, tensile and asphalt test results and flags samples that fall below specified strength.
